name: Portal Framework Authentication API
description:
This document describes the Authentication API of Portal Framework, an authentication API for CenturyLink portals. It comprises endpoints to obtain and handle session tokens, request user details and manage admin settings.
All authentication endpoints return two tokens: a refresh token and an access token. The refresh token is long lived, can be extended and can be used to obtain a new access token, whereas the access token is short lived, cannot be extended and cannot be used for authentication purposes.

The access token purpose is then to grant access to resource APIs. These tokens contain basic user details (see the `jwt_token` schema in the Identity API documentation). One such details is the `enterprise`: it may not be present (for users not linked to a Control Center account, include the default enterprise ID or, if requested with the `/token` endpoint using the `refresh_token` grant type, a specific enterprise ID. This token can be used by applications APIs to identify the enterprise on which the user is acting.

Applications may user endpoints under the **User information** section to obtain additional information about the user, such as Control Center user ID, default enterprise ID, linked enterprises and accounts, etc. These endpoints must be called with an access token.

Some of the identity endpoints as served with a different path when served behind an API gateway (production and beta, mainly). For instance, `/services/identity/profile` will be served on `/Enterprise/v1/Security/portalIdentity/profile`. In order to develop locally, those paths are also exposed as aliases of the main paths, so the client can be written to access the same paths as it will need to access in production or testing. Authorization and authentication are identical in both paths.
